packageRules.description: Routine updates are flagged for automerge, but be aware this has never actually fired — every dependency PR so far was merged by hand. GitHub's auto-merge is only offered on PRs blocked by something (required status checks or reviews) and this repo has neither, so Renovate falls back to its own automerge, which only runs when the weekly workflow runs. By then rebaseWhen has usually just rebased the branch and CI is pending again. The flag is kept because the intent is right: it starts working the moment either a more frequent Renovate cron or required status checks exist. The smoke-test groups below come after and override this back to manual for their packages.

Majors are adopted deliberately, and several are blocked upstream for months at a time (eslint 10 on eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y's peer range, typescript 7 on typescript-eslint's). An open PR for one of those sits untouched indefinitely, occupying a prConcurrentLimit slot and getting rebased plus fully re-tested every run. Queue them on the dependency dashboard instead: they stay visible as checkboxes and only become a branch when someone ticks one.
Pear runtime hosts the worker process; bump deliberately and smoke-test OTA, DMG, MSIX, AppImage, and native modules before merging
Holepunch P2P stack grouped so cross-package bumps land together; the integration test in test/raw/holepunch-integration.test.js is the merge gate
Electron drives the entire UI surface; smoke-test before merging

hyperdht 6.33.0 rewrote the LAN shortcut in lib/connect.js to race the LAN ping against holepunch, which degrades connection setup on the loopback testnet under Linux CI — every flow shard times out waiting for member-join-request while macOS passes (see issue #13). This cap constrains Renovate version LOOKUPS only. lockFileMaintenance does not look packages up — it hands npm a full re-resolve against the package.json ranges — so it ignored this rule and put 6.33.2 in the lock (PR #87, every flow shard red). The binding guard is the ~6.32.0 range plus the matching overrides entry in package.json; npm rejects the two disagreeing with EOVERRIDE, so they move together. Raise all three at once, and only after a Linux runner proves the newer version green.
